en.headline: CUHK Medical Centre apologises after doctor removes patient's ovaries by mistake
en.dek: The hospital said an experienced surgeon suffered a lapse in concentration during a September operation intended only to remove the uterus and fallopian tubes; the patient remains stable.
body: The Chinese University of Hong Kong Medical Centre has apologised after a 45-year-old patient’s ovaries were removed by mistake during surgery in September that was meant to remove only her uterus and fallopian tubes.

Hospital chief executive Chung Kin-lai said the doctor experienced a temporary lapse in concentration, failing to follow the agreed plan to preserve the ovaries. A nurse discovered the error while verifying specimens after the operation.

Professor Cheung Tak-hong, identified in media reports as the surgeon, said he accepts full responsibility for the basic error, which occurred when he focused too intently on the procedure and lost track of the original plan. The hospital said the patient is stable and will receive free follow-up care. The Department of Health listed the case as a sentinel event.

zh.headline: 中大醫院就醫生誤切病人卵巢致歉
zh.dek: 院方指經驗豐富的外科醫生在九月手術中短暫失神，原計劃只切除子宮及輸卵管，病人情況穩定。
body: 香港中文大學醫院就一名四十五歲女病人在九月手術中被誤切雙側卵巢致歉。該手術原計劃只切除子宮及雙側輸卵管。
醫院行政總裁鍾健禮表示，涉事醫生手術期間短暫失神，未能跟從保留卵巢的計劃。護士在術後核對標本時發現錯誤。
傳媒報道指涉事醫生為張德康教授，他表示願承擔全部責任，形容是基本錯誤，因手術時過於專注而偏離原計劃。院方稱病人情況穩定，將提供免費跟進治療。衞生署已將事件列為嚴重醫療事故。
